body.text: Fri, 11 Sept, 11:00 pm, Final score, IAW 117, AAW 4/121
Live updates: South Africa vs Australia, third Test, day three from Newlands, Cape Town
South Africa loses Aiden Markram and David Bedinham cheaply as Australia makes early inroads with the new ball.
Follow all the action in our live blog, check out the stats in our match Scorecard and ScoreCentre, and tune in to our live radio coverage.

19th over - Pat Cummins continues
Leg slip, slip and gully for Ackerman, who wastes no time in getting off strike with a single to point.
18th over - Lyon continues
Ackerman sweeps and will get a single. Looks to score quickly, Ackerman.

Marnus Labuschagne yelps for an LBW that not a single other person on the planet thought might have been even remotely close as Bavuma sweeps, the ball hitting him metres outside the line. Perhaps if he's judging the line that badly he should be dropped to grade cricket out at Redlands, let alone play for Queensland.
BEATEN! Bavuma defends a couple and then, facing the last ball of the over, steps back and delivers a fierce swish of the bat, but it misses the ball which is taken by Carey.
Cummins concerns
Agree Captain Pat needs a wicket or two before the selectors start to consider putting him in as an opener - Mike
Agree Captain Pat needs a wicket or two before the selectors start to consider putting him in as an opener
You are right Simon with your over heading. “Cummins needs a wicket”. last 2 innings he has 0-170 and no runs either this innings! Is he injured or just old?? - Dan
You are right Simon with your over heading. “Cummins needs a wicket”. last 2 innings he has 0-170 and no runs either this innings! Is he injured or just old??
I don't think he's too old.
I just think it hasn't quite happened for him in the last two Tests.
There's time for him to make a mark here.
17th over - Cummins continues
Bavuma defends outside off and lets out a yelp of "no" when he plays it.
A pleasing buzz around the ground from the healthy crowd.
BIG APPEAL! That's nipped back a bit and rapped Bavuma on the pads. It's always a chance of being low enough if it hits Bavuma's pads.
AND AUSTRALIA ARE GOING TO REVIEW!
It is a touch high... There's no bat involved, but it's hit him on the thigh pad. We await ball tracking.
And it's missing by a milimetre or two. Good decision. It is height that saves Bavuma. A fraction lower and it would have hit middle.
Bavuma pushes to cover and squeals "no" to stop the run.
Bavuma fends a shorter ball that rises up and he gets it away to fine leg.
That's 4,000 Test runs for Temba Bavuma and the Cape Town crowd sings his name in appreciation.
Ackerman fends away to fine leg for a single too.
And Bavuma ends the over with a defensive stroke.
16th over - Lyon will get through a mountain of work this session
Bavuma pushes back to Lyon with a flourish of his bat outside off stump.
Lyon has seen the rough and he wants to exploit it.
That turns a bit on its way in and Bavuma turns the ball to midwicket.
Watching spin bowling can be the most mesmerising of pastimes.
Dust puffs up there as Bavuma defends another that grips and bites a little bit.
Oh and that one kept low! That's a great line he's bowling, just four or five stump-widths outside of the off stump.
Bavuma defends another one.
And then he pushes away for a single off the final ball of the over to mid on.
15th over - Pat Cummins needs a wicket
Leg gully, first slip, and a gully.
EDGED! Off the inside half of the bat as well there, Ackerman tried to drive but missed out.
Off the outside half of the bat this time from Ackerman and he gets a single down to backward point.
Cummins bowls on the off stump, and Bavuma defends with a straight bat.
Outside off, left alone by Bavuma, who just needs a bit of time to settle here after the tea break. Hopefully his belly isn't as jumpy as his fast bowlers have been over the last couple of days.
Bavuma pushes into the cover point region for a single.
Ackerman defends the last.
There are a couple of clouds just drifting off the mountains further down the coast. Australia would love them to appear over the Table and roll in here, but it doesn't look likely at the moment.
14th over - Nathan Lyon will resume after tea
Slip and short leg for Lyon's bowling, Temba Bavuma is the batter at the strikers end of the wicket, and he defends before going on a little wander in a circle.
He levers the ball right into the man at short leg, who absorbs the blow and saves a run.
BIG TURN! That's a good one from Lyon. Outside off, huge puff of dust and it turns a long way towards leg.
BEATEN! And that one did not turn at all, Bavuma playing across the line a bit there and was lucky he didn't edge it or get cleaned up by it.
Bavuma defends into the leg side.
And then he gets forward and defends into the off.
Maiden to start, and an encouraging over for Australia.
Simon will return with the wickets after tea
Alright Simon. time to pull out your wicket-taking blog posts, I think we need at least four down today to be confident to wrap things up in the last couple of days. - Josh
Alright Simon. time to pull out your wicket-taking blog posts, I think we need at least four down today to be confident to wrap things up in the last couple of days.
I think you'll have more luck with Simon, Josh!
I actually went wicketless all of yesterday, although I've seen a few more so far today.
This series is a story of Markram's career

I wonder if Markram will be considering his series a bit of a missed opportunity. He's had a couple of 75+ scores and a couple of non-starts, feel like there was a chance for him to bat big but he didn't quite go the distance. He's still played very well though, better than another South African-born batter we could mention. The first Test in particular he did well to steady the ship - Josh

I wonder if Markram will be considering his series a bit of a missed opportunity. He's had a couple of 75+ scores and a couple of non-starts, feel like there was a chance for him to bat big but he didn't quite go the distance. He's still played very well though, better than another South African-born batter we could mention. The first Test in particular he did well to steady the ship
- Josh
Unfortunately, Josh, this series is a microcosm of Aiden Markram's career.
There are few openers around the world that are as easy on the eye as he is, but unfortunately he lacks the application to become truly, truly world class.
That's why his Test average is in the mid-30s rather than being in the mid-40s where it probably should be.
I can get around this one
Is it time to mention one of my pet lbw rule hates - if the ball is going to hit the stumps it should be out regardless of where it piches... - Mike
Is it time to mention one of my pet lbw rule hates - if the ball is going to hit the stumps it should be out regardless of where it piches...
- Mike
You know what? I agree with you, Mike.
Enough of this 'umpire's call' baloney.
Key Event
TEA: South Africa 2-53 (Ackerman 33, Bavuma 4)
South Africa goes into the break trailing by 47 runs with eight wickets in hand.
There was a little bit on offer for the Australian quicks with the new ball, but South Africa will be disappointed with the dismissals of both Aiden Markram and David Bedingham.
They'll need much more application from the other batters if they're to set a competitive total for the Aussies.
This partnership will be the major key, you'd think. Ackerman is the form man from the first innings, and has looked solid, and we know how hard Bavuma is to dislodge once he gets set.
South Africa bats deep, right down to Simon Harmer at No.9 and they'll need each of their batters to pull their weight.
Australia in the driver's seat heading into the break and they'll know a strong final session could set them up for a win tomorrow.
Still a bit of work to do though for the tourists.
13th over - Ackerman is almost run out before tea
Cummins over the wicket to Bavuma, who again punches one into the off-side and calls Ackerman through for a single.
He comes around to Ackerman.
The first one is pitched outside off and Ackerman punches it into the off side, but straight to the fielder.
A well-directed short ball next up from Cummins, but Ackerman decisively ducks under it.

RUN OUT CHANCE! Ackerman knocks it into the off side and sets off for a run, but is sent back by Bavuma! Connolly picks it up and has a shy at the stumps and Ackerman had given up, but the throw is wide.
Another short delivery, this one goes through a little lower and surprises Ackerman a bit, but he's able to dodge it once again.
Cummins finishes up with a full one and Ackerman drives to mid-off and that's tea. My goodness, that would've been a devastating way to end the session for the Proteas but they dodge a bullet.
12th over - Lyon replaces Hazlewood in the attack
We get our first look at Lyon. He's over the wicket to Bavuma.
The first one is on off stump and doesn't spin much and Bavuma defends into the leg side.
The second one is on a similar line but spins a little more and Temba knocks it into the on side again.
Lyon gets wider outside off next and Bavuma leans forward and defends.
The next one is whizzed in a little quicker and Bavuma defends once again, in less convincing fashion.
Bavuma rocks back and punches the next one into the off side and picks up a single.
Lyon comes around the wicket to Ackerman.
BIG LBW APPEAL! Lyon beats Ackerman all ends up with one that seems to go on with the arm, but the umpire is unmoved.
Cummins decides to send it upstairs.
It looks like it's beaten the bat and has hit Ackerman in the back leg.
Ball tracking shows that it's hit Ackerman outside the line, so the review is unsuccessful. Good decision from Richard Illingworth.
11th over - Ackerman rides his luck against Cummins
Cummins starts over the wicket to Ackerman and pitches one on middle and length and is defended into the off side.
FOUR! EDGED! Cummins drops it a little shorter and Ackerman flashes at it and sends the ball flying over the slips cordon.
Cummins goes a back of a length outside off, but Ackerman isn't tempted this time, wisely leaves it alone.
Another short one and Ackerman again pulls well in front of square and picks up two to the man in the deep. In good control of that shot so far today.
Cummins comes around the wicket to change up the angle.
BEATEN! Better area from Cummins, in that corridor of uncertainty and beats Ackerman's defensive prod all ends up.
A similar delivery but this time Ackerman is able to work it to the leg side and he picks up another pair of runs, good running that time.
10th over - Neser makes a mess of Hazlewood's over
Hazlewood continues around the wicket to Ackerman, who chops the first one into the off side for a dot. Tidy stuff.
A bit of a teaser from Hazlewood, wider outside off, but Ackerman shoulders arms.
Ackerman tries to drive the next one through the covers, but mistimes it to the man at stationed at point.
FOUR! Hazlewood digs it in short and Ackerman pulls well. Neser, the sub fielder, looks like he's got it covered on the boundary, but then makes an absolute meal of things.
Fuller from Hazlewood, honing in on leg stump and Ackerman on drives but can't beat mid-on.
Another short one from Hazlewood, this time from over the wicket, and Ackerman pulls it in front of square for a single to end the over.
9th over - Cummins replaces Starc in the attack
Australia's captain brings himself into the attack looking to end an uncharacteristic wicket drought. Bavuma on strike to start the over.
The first ball is wide outside off stump and Bavuma shoulders arms.
Cummins gets a little closer to off stump with the next one and has Bavuma defending into the off side.
A little shorter from Cummins and Bavuma punches it off the back foot and picks up a single.
Cummins stays over the wicket to Ackerman, who punches one pitched on middle stump on a good length to mid off.
A short one from Cummins over leg stump, but Ackerman is able to duck under it easily.
Ackerman guides the next one past backward point and picks up another single to move into the 20s.
8th over cont. - Bavuma arrives at the crease
The South African captain Temba Bavuma arrives at the crease with a mountain of work to do.
Two poor shots have seen two dismissals so far. Nowhere near the level of application required out there from the Proteas.

CLOSE! My goodness! Bavuma drops it into the off-side and calls Ackerman through for a quick single and Ackerman is almost run out! Josh Inglis with the good pick-up and shy at the stumps, but he misses.
Hazlewood comes around the wicket to Ackerman and bounces him first up, and Ackerman ducks under it easily.
FOUR! Great shot from Ackerman! He walks down the track at Hazlewood ever so slightly and guides it past backward point for a pressure release boundary.
Key Event
WICKET! Bedingham holes out in the deep!
This is a tremendously poor shot from David Bedingham!
Hazlewood digs it in short and Bedingham tries to take it on despite there being two men out in the deep.
Nathan Lyon takes the easy catch and South Africa are in trouble here.
David Bedingham 11 (16) c Lyon b Hazlewood, FOW: 2-31
8th over - Hazlewood into his fourth over
BEATEN! Terrific delivery from Hazlewood. It's just outside off stump and seams away after pitching, beating Bedingham's forward defence.
A similar delivery, but this time Bedingham meets it with the full face of the bat, defending into the covers.
7th over - Starc roughs up Bedingham with a short one
FOUR! Shot! Starc too full that time, that's in the slot and Bedingham leans into a wonderful cover drive and beats the sweeper in the deep as well, that's how well he's timed that.
BEATEN! Great response from Starc as he drags his length back a tad and seams one across Bedingham, beating his defensive prod all ends up.
Another one in the slot from Starc which Bedingham absolutely smokes, but he's hit it straight to the man at cover. Good shot for no runs.
OUCH! A brute of a bouncer from Starc at 143.4 kph! It gets really big on Bedingham and thuds into his chest. He's done really well to get his gloves out of the way of that one.
This one is short, but not as short as the previous one, and Bedingham rocks back and defends.
Another short one on the leg side and Bedingham negotiates it well, guiding it down to fine leg for a single to end the over.
Starc coming off the ground after that over and he's being replaced by Michael Neser.
6th over - Hazlewood into his third over
Hazlewood stays over the wicket to Ackerman and pitches one on middle on a back of a length and dots up the left-hander.
CLOSE! Ackerman misses an attempted pull shot and the ball almost dribbles onto his stumps after hitting his thigh pad. A bit of uneven pace that time.
Another one on a back of a length, but this time it's leg-sided and Ackerman works it away for a single onto the leg side.
Hazlewood hits a lovely length just outside Bedingham's off stump and Bedingham drops it into the off side and calls Ackerman through for a quick single. Good running.
Hazlewood comes around the wicket and angles one into Ackerman's pads and he works it away through the leg side for a single.

Floated up and Bedingham goes for a big drive through the covers and wants two initially but Ackerman sends him back so they've got to settle for a single. A little bit of a mix-up between the two, but Bedingham makes it back safely at hte non-striker's end.
5th over - Starc fights through despite injury scare
Starts with a wide yorker which Bedingham squeezes out into the covers.
Let's see how freely Starc moves with that little calf niggle we saw at the end of the last over.
Strays into the hips and Bedingham works it away for an easy single on the leg side.
Full and straight and Ackerman meets it with a lovely on drive but can't quite beat the man at mid-on.
FOUR BYES! Starc digs it in and this one goes flying way over Ackerman's head and Carey's got no chance. 141.9 kph from the left-armer.
Straight and back of a length from Starc at 146 kph and Ackerman is defending on the back foot.
Another well-directed short one from Starc, but Ackerman deals with it well, drops it into the leg side and picks up a quick single to end the over.
4th over - Hazlewood is going to continue
Bedingham drives away for a single. Starc is still limping around back there, feeling at his calf.
BEATEN! Oh what a ball. On the rise outside off, a little bit of nip and that takes it away from the fending blade.
Ackerman drives to cover and takes a single. Busy batter, is Ackerman. Looks hard to bat out there all of a sudden.
Bedingham defends into the cover point region and will take a very comfortable single.
Leg gully comes in and Hazlewood delivers a bouncer, Ackerman ducks under it.
Solid defence ends the over.
Now, will Mitch Starc take the ball for a third over? Chris de Silva will tell you all about it.
3rd over - Starc has one more, but then limps away at the end of the over
David Bedingham has one ball to face.
He plays it to point and takes a single to get off the mark.
Mitch Starc walks down to his fielding position. And he is limping. And grimacing... Uh oh...
Key Event
OUT! MARKRAM IS OUT!
A soft dismissal there for Aidan Markram.
He has driven the ball on the up, hitting it straight to Travis Head at mid off, who didn't have to move!
Sloppy dismissal for the opener.
And all of a sudden Australia will be thinking they are a real chance to make some inroads before tea.
Australia still leads by 88 runs.
Aiden Markram 1 (6) c Head b Starc, FOW: 1-12
3rd over - Starc continues
So, how much more swing are we going to see?

FOUR! Oh boy. That's a great shot, upright and punching backward of point. It's just a bit short, but Ackerman used the bounce and the pace to keep the ball down and played it safely past a motionless gully.
He leaves the next.
Ackerman fends a shorter one into the backward point region and takes a single.
Markram drives to mid off but there is no run.
2nd over - Josh Hazlewood comes into the attack
The hammer is out, just breaking down some of the ridges around the landing zone that Hazlewood will be planting his giant feet into in a few short moments time.
BEATEN! A beauty from Hazlewood, rising outside off, across the face of Ackerman and beating the outside edge.
Two slips and a leg slip in place.
FOUR! Off the outside edge between second slip and gully for a third-man boundary.
Ackerman defends off his stumps, a positive looking defensive stroke, wanting to push forward.

HIT HIM! Right on the hand and chest area. As we keep getting reminded on the Fox TV coverage, batting can be dangerous and one can sometimes expect to get ready for a broken arm. That is just an awkward one. Steep bounce, Ackerman didn't know where he wanted to be and is struck on the hand and chest there.
BEATEN! Hazlewood has the ball on a string, wobble seam and across Ackerman, beating the outside edge. Superb follow up from the bouncer. Pain, followed by precision.
Ackerman clips the last off his leg for a single to fine leg.
Cummins to be the destroyer?
This test keeps us all guessing about what next. I see the Aussies taking 3/50 .earlyish with Cummo doing the damage - Chris in Budapest.
This test keeps us all guessing about what next. I see the Aussies taking 3/50 .earlyish with Cummo doing the damage
- Chris in Budapest.
I mean, he is due...
1st over - Mitch Starc with the new ball
I mean, who else?
Is he going to swing it? All eyes on these first deliveries...
Three slips and a gully, Markram attempts to drive into the off side, but can't time his shot and it falls just down in front of him. Bit short, no swing.
That was a bit fuller, and a bit of swing into the right handed batter from over the wicket.
BIG APPEAL! Starc likes it - nobody else does. There was swing, good swing for Starc and that did come back into him. It's very high so they won't go upstairs.
Off the mark for Markram, a bit short and he pushes to deep point for a single.
Left-hander on deck now, Ackerman fresh off 95 in the first innings. Three slips and a gully, Ackerman defends off his pads.
Ackerman gets off the mark by pushing into the covers for a swift single.
Is 100 enough?
100., oh well see how it goes - Peter
100., oh well see how it goes
- Peter
It is so hard to know.
Everything, and I don't think I am being overly dramatic here, comes down to whether this new ball will swing.
If it does, giddy up, because South Africa's batters might be in a bit of strife - and that 100 run lead will look very impressive.

If South Africa can bat and make, say, 300 for a lead of 200, chasing that on days four and five might be a bit problematic for the Aussies - if the South African bowlers are fully fit after a monumental effort over the past couple of days - and some stomach issues.
Key Event
Australia all out for 429, lead of 100
Australia has a lead, a very, very good lead, of 100 runs after being bowled out for 429.
It's perhaps not as much as they might have hoped.
But this pitch does just look as though it is starting to do something here.
There's been a couple of puffs of dust off the deck and, with that ball at least, there has been some reverse swing that made a huge difference.
Any sort of swing may end up being the difference here.
Australia in the box seat? You'd think so.
Key Event
CAUGHT AND BOWLED JANSEN!
Connolly drives!
Jansen leans down and catches it in his follow through.
And that is the end of that!
Cooper Connolly 29 (83) c&b Jansen, FOW: 10-429
126th over - Janson comes in again
125th over - More from Mulder
Josh Hazlewood is the new man in.
FOUR! And he crushes the first ball he faces to the cover boundary! He played a long way from his body, all hands and no feet but perfectly timed. No swing for Mulder and it cost him a boundary.
The lead is 100
Hazlewood drives to cover, who makes a stop this time.
Hazlewood defends on his stumps.
Key Event
EDGED! GOT HIM!
Brilliant outswinger from Wiaan Mulder and Simon Harmer takes the catch at second slip.
That's great bowling, once he found his groove, Mulder persisted and got the swinging ball to sing to him.
Nathan Lyon 1 (25) c Harmer b Mulder, FOW: 9-425
125th over - Mulder continues
Lyon is on strike and he defends the first.
Good yorker from Mulder there, Lyon doing very well to keep it out, but keep it out he does, nicely played by Lyon.
Hmmm, food...
Reassuring to hear Shaun Pollock and (I think) Ben Cameron on the ABC coverage talking about food and test venues around the world, let’s hope it stays uneventful on the field… - Mike
Reassuring to hear Shaun Pollock and (I think) Ben Cameron on the ABC coverage talking about food and test venues around the world, let’s hope it stays uneventful on the field…
- Mike
124th over - Jansen continues
Around the wicket for Jansen, and Connolly has to get up on his toes to fend the ball down in front of him. The field is spread so it's very safe to do so, although there is a bat pad.
Bouncer again, but that one didn't get up too high and Connolly almost got a chest rub from that one as he leaned back away from it.
Another bouncer, but Connolly is having to duck and the ball is barely getting over him.
Over the wicket from Jansen.

GOT HIM! That's hit him hard and Connolly ducked right into it. That's hit the helmet with a fearsome clunk. That's hit him absolutely flush on the badge. Jansen's first instinct is to walk away but once the medical staff come out he does have a look and says something. They'll conduct their checks and make sure the youngster is OK to continue.
And it seems that he is.
I wonder where this next ball is going to go from Jansen?
Right up at the chin, and Connolly wants to run to get off strike but some good fielding keeps him in the blockhole.
I wonder where this next ball is going to go?
Another bouncer, chest height, and Connolly has to fend it away just in front of bat pad. That's great pace bowling from Jansen.
123rd over - Wiaan Mulder comes in again
Again, I know Rabada is ill, but Mulder is not the play here.
Nathan Lyon defends solidly.

EDGED! DOWN! Lyon edges to second slip, Harmer falls away to his right and the ball just doesn't carry to Simon Harmer! He couldn't be much closer than he already is, but that's so unfortunate for Simon Harmer and the South Africans.
BEATEN! Good ball from Mulder, who I feel sorry for doubting now. That ball moved away a little and Lyon just dangled the bat outside the line.
BEATEN AGAIN! Great ball, same as the last. Lyon is now edgy.
Lyon fends to backward point, a more confident stroke that time.
Another better push from Lyon outside off. Well negotiated in the end.
122nd over - Marco Jansen is coming in once again
Connolly cuts, a lovely square shot but no run taken.
I can't help but think Connolly could, and should, trust Nathan Lyon a bit more here. He's a competent batter and can hold up an end if he needs to.
FOUR! That's a very good shot from Connolly, driving past cover and the ball races away to the boundary.
Jansen is going to come around the wicket, I fear young Cooper Connolly is going to get some chin music for his impudence at hitting that shot and failing to run all that much.
Bouncer, Connolly leans his head back nonchalantly. That's unlikely to help Jansen's mood.
APPEAL! Big yorker! A good yorker. His appeals need work - it was just a little shout more than anything. Also, Connolly hit that with the middle of the base of his bat. Not out.
A bouncer ends the over - keeps Nathan Lyon on strike at the other end.
121st over - Mulder continues
Connolly clips to wide mid on for no run.
Connolly clips away to midwicket. No run.
Connolly drives to point, again no run is taken.
The brakes have been firmly put on here.
Connolly clips off his pads and he will take a run this time down to deep backward square leg.
Wiaan Mulder has bowled with nothing like the intensity required here so far.
Two nothing balls to Lyon ends the over and South Africa needs to change something here.
120th over - Jansen continues
Connolly drives to cover - there's a run available there but they don't take it.
Connolly cuts to wide third man, no run taken again.
Left on length by Connolly. A tight leave but a good leave.
Down the leg side, off Connolly's pad but well taken by a tumbling Rickelton...
Down the leg side again, a leg bye is taken this time as the ball dribbles away to backward square leg.
Lyon leaves the one ball he is allowed to face.
119th over - Wiaan Mulder from the other end
I just don't think this is the play for South Africa.
Mulder drops short, a half volley for Connolly outside off and he takes advantage with a push into the covers for a couple.
Left outside off, there is a gasp from the crowd that ripples around like the heat haze in Cape Town, but there was little to get excited about there.
Driven to mid off for no run that time by Connolly.
Too straight, Connolly takes a single into the leg side.
Two balls for Lyon, who is hardly a bunny down at number 10.
BEATEN! That's a great ball from Mulder, Lyon just prodding forward a little and the ball fizzing past the outside of the bat.
FOUR! Down the leg side, horrible bowling from Mulder, and it will be byes. Ryan Rickelton didn't have much chance but he perhaps could have done better - he did get glove to it.
118th over - Marco Jansen comes into the attack
He's not been all that well, Marco Jansen, which is why he's not had a lot of overs - just four in that first session. He needs to bowl well here.
Two slips, a gully, Connolly pushes into the covers but turns down the run. Australia's lead is 82.
Oh there's a bit of swing there, going down towards leg and hitting Connolly on the pad.
More reverse swing, better starting line and Connolly drives to cover for no run.
Outside off, left alone by Connolly.
Connolly defends a back of a length delivery off the inside edge of his bat onto his pads.
Connolly pulls a short one and it's high into the leg side - it will fall safe and they will run a single.
What lead will Australia be searching for?
Need to try scrape through another session here and get 150 ahead. Cannot imagine batting last is gonna be great. - Chris
Need to try scrape through another session here and get 150 ahead. Cannot imagine batting last is gonna be great.
- Chris
120 or more? - Peter
120 or more?
- Peter
It's the big question, how many more can Australia get with two wickets in hand?
I wonder whether Connolly comes out and chances his arm a little after the lunch break to try and add to the lead.
The pitch is still playing well, so Australia would love to get to somewhere around the 150-run mark, considering they've got to bat last on this pitch.
The conditions may be batter-friendly right now, but I promise you, it'll be nasty out here on day five when Australia has to bat in the fourth innings.
South Africa far from out of this contest.
WBBL: Thunder beat the Renegades
The Sydney Thunder have got their WBBL season off to a winning start, beating the Melbourne Renegades by six wickets at Junction Oval.
The Thunder chased down the Renegades' total of 138 with 18 balls to spare.
Thunder number three batter Anika Learoyd scored 48 off 37 balls, building on Georgia Voll (25) and Phoebe Litchfield's (17) 34-run opening partnership.
Her innings came to a halt when Tayla Vlaeminck, bowling with real pace, bowled her to claim a first WBBL wicket in five years.
Hayley Matthews scored 45 off 30 balls at the top of the order for the Rengades, but Voll's 4-26 with the ball underlined a genuine all-rounder's opponent.
Sheffield Shield: Wickets tumble at Adelaide Oval
What a bizarre game of cricket going on at Adelaide Oval.
Only three wickets fell on day one, as Western Australia powered to a score that would eventually be 5-406, Cameron Bancroft scoring 186 for WA.
Good pitch?
Apparently not one that would last more than a day, with 18 wickets falling on day two.
South Australia were bowled out for 154, Jhye Richardson taking 3-29, including two in two balls (and he was unlucky not to get an LBW decision for a hat-trick in truth).
Then, WA were reduced to 6-79, Brendan Doggett taking 3-19.
WA do still have a commanding lead of 331 runs in the match and, with the bowlers suddenly discovering something, you'd back them in from here.
Alex Carey loves the Sheffield Shield
If you couldn't love him enough anyway, all round Aussie nice guy Alex Carey has told ABC Sport that he loves the Sheffield Shield, which he helped South Australia win last year.
Loving first class cricket clearly makes you a great person.
But how has his state done in the opening match of round three? Let's have a look, shall we?
Key Event
LUNCH: Australia 8-411 (Connolly 20, Lyon 1)
A fascinating session in the books with the ledger reading 4-81 in the end from 27 overs.
South Africa will be happy to have made some inroads, but they won't want the Aussies to grab a lead of much more than 100.
The conditions for batting still appear to be very good, but with this pitch getting more and more abrasive, Nathan Lyon will become a factor in the third innings.
Cooper Connolly has looked a little streaky so far, but he's still out there, while Lyon looks as solid as ever with the bat.
I wonder whether we see more of Marco Jansen after lunch with South Africa needing to wrap this thing up without much more damage.
The highlight of the opening session was Josh Inglis making his second Test ton, but unfortunately for Australia, he wasn't able to kick on and make it a big one.
South Africa did well to remove Alex Carey shortly afterwards as well, getting some new batters at the crease.
117th over - Harmer bowls the final over before lunch
Tosses up the first one outside off but Lyon reaches forward and defends solidly.
He works the next one away into the leg side but lets out a big "NO!" to Connolly, who considers a single.
Another delivery outside off from Harmer and Lyon again defends.
He goes wider with this one and Lyon reaches forward and defends. The fielders behind the stumps are trying to goad him into a big shot here.
Harmer goes around the wicket and pitches it on middle and Lyon drives him down the wicket.
A fuller delivery and Lyon defends and that's lunch!
116th over - Coetzee keeps things tight against Connolly
Coetzee stays around the wicket to Connolly, who leaves the first one alone as it pitches wide outside off stump.
I'd be going to Jansen here with just a few minutes left before lunch, if I'm Bavuma.
Connolly with a big drive into the deep past backward point, but turns down the single again to protect Lyon from the paceman.
A good short one from Coetzee, a little down the leg side though and Connolly ducks under comfortably.
Coetzee pitches one on the back of a length on a middle stump line and Connolly defends down the pitch.
A good delivery, this time a little fuller, and Connolly defends it down the pitch again. That one looked much quicker.
A bouncer to end the over and Connolly ducks under it once again to give the Proteas a full over at Lyon next up.
115th over - Connolly survives big LBW shout
LBW APPEAL! Harmer gets one to go on with the arm and strikes Connolly on the pads, but that's going down leg.
A full delivery next up and Harmer fields well off his own bowling to deny a single.
Another one aimed at middle and leg and Harmer again dives to keep Connolly on strike after a strong drive.
Harmer goes a bit shorter and Connolly drives well to keep it out, but can't get off strike.
Floated up and Connolly punches off the back foot to pick up a single.
Lyon with one ball to negotiate.
Harmer flights one outside off and Lyon drives off the back foot but it's a dot ball to end the over.
114th over - Connolly lives dangerously against Coetzee
Ryan Rickelton has just denied a proposal from a man in the crowd to his mum.
EDGED! Coetzee goes full outside off and catches the edge of Connolly's bat, but the ball doesn't quite carry to Aiden Markram at second slip.
Driven uppishly from Connolly to the man in the deep and we've got some strike farming because he turns down the single.
A slower one from Coetzee outside off and Connolly initially attempts a drive, but then pulls out in the nick of time.
FOUR! How's he dug this out?! Coetzee with a lovely inswinging yorker and Connolly gets his bat down and times it impeccably as it whizzes through the covers.
Coetzee bangs the next one in short, but it's down the leg side, easily left alone.
Another good length delivery but Connolly picks up a single to end the over to retain the strike.
113th over - Harmer sizes up Lyon
We've got some offie on offie crime happening as Harmer sizes up Lyon.
He starts over the wicket and spins one into Lyon's pads and Lyon whips him away for a single on the leg side.
Around the wicket to Connolly next up, and he defends a good delivery on middle stump.
An identical delivery again, good drift from Harmer and Connolly once again defends.
He gets outside off with the next one and draws a big drive out of Connolly, who picks up a single to the man in the deep.
A good delivery pitching outside off and Lyon leans forward and defends well.
This one goes on with the arm a little and Lyon defends on the back foot this time.
112th over cont. - Lyon arrives at the crease
Nathan Lyon is the new man at the crease. He can prove to be a very annoying tailender on his day, always puts a high price on his wicket.
Coetzee starts over the wicket to the right-hander.
Swings one in towards middle and leg and the ball thuds off Lyon's thigh pad into the leg side and he picks up a leg bye.
He goes around the wicket to Connolly, but this one is too wide and Connolly shoulders arms easily.
A good full length delivery to end the over which Connolly digs out.
Key Event
WICKET! Coetzee nicks Starc off!
Gerald Coetzee is finally on the board and he is rapt!
A good length delivery just outside off and he draws the rash drive out of Mitchell Starc, and Starc only succeeds in nick it through to Ryan Rickelton.
Coetzee smacks his own head in frustration and celebration, an important wicket that!
Mitchell Starc c Rickelton b Coetzee 11 (29), FOW: 8-402
112th over - Coetzee to continue
This has developed into another handy partnership for the Aussies, it's now up to 22 runs.
Coetzee stays over the wicket to Connolly and pitches it on middle and off and Connolly dabs it into the off side to pick up a single.
Coetzee around the wicket to Starc who defends one on the off side.
111th over - Starc breaks free against Harmer
Harmer resumes his battle with Starc, who has remained very patient thus far.
Floats another one in on middle stump and Starc drives into the covers.
FOUR! A bit of width that time and Starc rocks back and cuts it through backward point and that takes Australia past the 400-run mark.
A similar length, but the line is better next up and Starc is dotted up.
Gets fuller with the next one and Starc is forward and defending.
Another shorter one from Harmer, a little quicker, and Starc defends on the back foot.
Floated up, that's better from Harmer, and Starc defends on the front foot. He's got to be there, not short.
110th over - Coetzee changes things up to left-handers
Can Coetzee get his lines right here? South Africa needs him to, with Australia's lead already at 67.
BEATEN! Floats one full and wide and gets the drive out of Starc, who plays and misses with his wild-looking shot.
Bavuma spots some loose thread on the ball and gets the umpires to slice it off.
A better area from Coetzee and Starc gets inside the line and defends into the off side.
Short from Coetzee, but the line isn't right and it's left alone. Just 137.9 kph, his pace is definitely down from yesterday.
The next one is closer to off stump but Starc again backs away a little and picks up a single to the sweeper on the off side.
Coetzee comes over the wicket to Connolly and tests him with a short one, but Connolly sways under it easily.
BEATEN! That's the length! Pitches it on middle and it swings away and whooshes past Connolly's big cover drive attempt.
109th over - Harmer continues to keep things tight
Harmer pitches one in middle and Connolly drives nicely down the ground for a single.
Good flight again from Harmer, pitching on middle and Starc reaches forward and defends.
A similar delivery again and Starc drives it straight to the man in the covers.
Slower from Harmer that time and Starc dabs it down to short third man and picks up a quick single, good running!
Harmer angles one into off stump and Connolly defends on the front foot.
This one is aimed at middle and Connolly again defends. Another tight over from Harmer, who's got 4-97 off 33 overs now.
108th over - Coetzee replaces Rabada in the attack
Gerald Coetzee has his first chance to go at the batters this morning, replacing Rabada.
He starts around the wicket to Connolly. I wonder whether he'll get some of that reverse as well.
FOUR! Full and wide, poor delivery, that's a 127.9 kph loosener and Connolly frees his hands and flays it over backward point.
Better from Coetzee, but still too much width and Connolly swats it away for a single to the man at deep point.
EDGED! FOUR! Unlucky! Good delivery from Coetzee, he catches the edge from Starc, but this one flies through the vacant third slip region.
Wider again from Coetzee and Starc leaves it alone this time. Australia's lead now up to 65.
Shorter from Coetzee, but it's again too wide and Starc is able to leave it easily.
Real wide again from Coetzee to end the over, he's not gotten into his rhythm yet. Starc again leaves.
107th over - Harmer continues to tempt Starc
Harmer staying around the wicket as he comes in to Connolly for his 32nd over of the innings.
The first one pitches on middle and Connolly defends it down the pitch on the back foot.
Lovely flight from Harmer, getting the ball to drive towards leg stump and Connolly defends on the front foot this time.
Full from Harmer and Connolly knocks it down to mid-on for a quick single, good running.
Floats it up outside off, trying to tempt Starc, but Starc defends into the off side.
Floated up again, but it's too full. Starc picks up a single down to long-off.
Lovely flight from Harmer to end the over! It's another big tempter it's met with a lovely leave. Good cricket all around.
106th over - Rabada to continue after breakthrough
Rabada continuing his spell. He looked really unwell during the DRS review for the Cummins wicket.
He's around the wicket to start to Connolly and sends the first one down leg side where Connolly misses an attempted flick.
A good length delivery just outside off and Connolly knocks it into the off side and picks up a single. Not sure why they don't bring the man up there.
CLOSE! Rabada swings one in to Starc and my goodness, that's so close to knocking him over. It actually swung too much and hit Starc on the pads before squeaking past leg stump.
Angled in towards middle and leg again, this time it's fuller, and Starc clips it away to get off the mark.
Looks like Rabada is getting some reverse swing here.
This one pitches and seams away from Connolly, and he knocks it to the man in the deep on the off side and picks up another easy single.
Another in-dipper from Rabada and this time Starc drives it well down the pitch, but Rabada fields in his follow-through.
105th over - Harmer continues as Starc arrives at the crease
Taking over from Mr. Smale for the remainder of this session and suddenly we've got a contest once again!
Mitchell Starc is the new man at the crease after the dismissal of Pat Cummins, but he won't be on strike just yet.
Harmer continuing what has been a brilliant spell as he sizes up Connolly.
The first one pitches on off stump and Connolly drives to the man in the covers.
Harmer goes a little straighter next up and Connolly drives down through mid-off for a single.
Yorker length from Harmer on middle stump to Starc, who digs it out back down the pitch.
Better length that time, gets Starc reaching and defending down the pitch.
CLOSE! Pitches it shorter and it skids through and Starc juuust gets the bat down in the nick of time.
Harmer tosses up the final delivery of the over and Starc drives to the man in the covers. A good over once again from the offie.
Key Event
LBW! PAT CUMMINS IS GIVEN OUT!
The finger went straight up there from Richard Illingworth. Looked good live. The ball darted in a little and hit Cummins right on the knee roll.
He did get a bit of a hop on though.
There's no bat involved. I think this will be umpires call.
IT'S UMPIRES CALL! Cummins is out!
It's just clipping the top of leg stump.
Right, that's enough from me, Chris de Silva will take you through to lunch.
Pat Cummins 0 (6) LBW b Rabada, FOW 7-380
104th over - Rabada carries on
Good ball, outside off and Cooper Connolly hasn't looked entirely comfortable out there, and doesn't look so there either, as the ball goes outside him.
Connolly fends to point and will take a single.
Good ball, and quick from Rabada to Cummins. 145km/h that has Cummins looking a bit uncomfortable.
Down the leg side from Rabada, and Cummins flicks his bat towards it without making contact.
Two slips and a gully in place. Leg slip comes in too.
Bit of dart in off the surface then from outside off, Cummins doing pretty well to get bat on it and keep it out.
103rd over - one to come, Pat Cummins to face it
And Cummins defends solidly after that quick drink.
Key Event
EDGED! ALEX CAREY HAS TO GO!
That's excellent!
Simon Harmer with the turn, drifting in and dipping. It catches the outside edge and goes straight to slip! Aiden Markram with a very good catch low down.
It's been a great innings for Alex Carey, and it took a very good ball to get him out.
Another huge wicket for South Africa!
Time for a drink.
Alex Carey 80 (186) c Markram b Harmer, FOW: 6-379
103rd over - Simon Harmer continues
Carey defends the first couple that are angled towards his stumps from around the wicket.
There's a slip and a leg slip in place.
102nd over - Rabada carries on
And stars by pegging a ball straight into the midriff of Alex Carey, who walks away taking a deep breath or two, no doubt.
Outside off, Rabada steaming in to bowl at 140km/h but not forcing Carey to play at the ball.
Carey check-pulls the ball to midwicket for a single.
BEATEN! Good ball, again Connolly betraying some nerves by fending at the ball as it fizzes past outside off.
Bouncer, Connolly ducks under it. Bit of a waste from Rabada.
He leaves the last alone outside off, and earns a visual rebuke from the South African quick, who remains wicketless.
101st over - Harmer continues
And Carey drives to mid off for a single.
CLOSE! Good ball from Harmer, getting Connolly stretching forward to defend the ball.
CLOSE! Another good ball there from Harmer, an inside edge saving Connolly from LBW.
There's an appeal from Rickelton, but not sure why. Connolly gets a bit of bat on that ball before it hits the pad, a sweep well stopped by Bedingham.
Connolly defends.
Good over, but well negotiated in the end.
100th over - Rabada continues
FOUR! Carey clips the ball off the toe end on the bat, past the slips to the third man boundary. More frustration for South Africa.
Carey drives square on the up, a single out to deep point.
Cooper Connolly, the new man, is going to be introduced to the batting crease by Kagiso Rabada.
Outside off, Connolly doesn't chase it and leaves well alone.
There are two slips and a gully in place.
BEATEN! That's close, a rising ball that Connolly fends at outside off. He was close to getting a touch on that one. Rabada stares at the youngster.
Now he's off the mark, a nice push into the covers for a single.
Carey pushes to deep point for a single to end the over.
Key Event
EDGED! TAKEN! JOSH INGLIS IS OUT!
Brilliant ball from Simon Harmer!
Drift away, that had Inglis reaching for the ball outside off, and then the turn back in.
He gets a feather of an edge to it and the ball nestles in the gloves of Ryan Rickelton.
A superb innings comes to an end and finally South Africa breaks this partnership.
Josh Inglis 102 (135) c Rickelton b Harmer, FOW 5-362
99th over - Harmer continues
Inglis defends the next ball into the off side..
And then he clips away for a single.
Carey paddle sweeps over to fine leg for a couple - and South Africa move a leg slip in to respond to that - a bit like trying to put the horses back in the paddock.
Now he runs a single.
Key Event
Hundred for Josh Inglis!
What a lovely shot from Josh Inglis to bring up his second Test century.
He's played as well as anyone has in this series by delivering this innings.
Perfectly timed, always looking to score but never reckless and that reverse sweep has been a perfect example of that.
101 runs off 132 balls.
Well played.
99th over - A bloodied Simon Harmer is coming into the attack
Small mercies for South Africa, it was not his bowling hand that got smashed up there.
He is going to come into the attack with that finger absolutely throbbing in pain.
FOUR! What a shot from Josh Inglis!
98th over - Kagiso Rabada gets a cheer as he's announced to return to the attack
OK, so we're told that Rabada didn't bowl straight away because he had been off the field late yesterday.
My word, South Africa need a big bowling performance from their key striker here. A massive moment in this first hour, that so far has been going very well for Australia.
Inglis clips off his hip for a single straight away.
Carey defends the next couple.
A bit of excitement there as Carey has to flinch away from a 140km/h shorter ball that rears up past Carey's head.
Solid defence there from Carey, another rising ball outside off.

EDGED! DROPPED IS IT? Four for Alex Carey as he edges past slip to third man. It did carry to Harmer at second slip. A hugely tough chance, and he's split the nail in attempting to make the catch. It was dying on him, it came at tremendous pace. He's bled for the cause, Simon Harmer, but there's no wicket at the end of it.
Good areas
97th over - Jansen is going to continue
Jansen and Bavuma are having a little chat before this over gets underway.
FOUR! It probably wasn't about doing this... Gorgeous shot from Carey, outside off, Carey driving on the up safe in the knowledge that the bounce will be true. Good shot.
Perhaps this is what the chat was about, a change in the field, bouncer barrage is coming I'd think...
Carey clips off his pads for a single.
Jansen bowls a full toss outside off which is fended away for a single to backward point.
Carey defends.
OH! Horrible full toss from Jansen! And a no ball. That just slipped out of his hand. He gets a warning, as you'd expect, but it wasn't intentional.
Bouncer this time as Jansen over-compensates and Carey ducks under it.
Carey defends the last.
96th over - Mulder continues
Inglis is rapped on the pad and will run a leg bye. Not a great ball.
He was over the wicket to Inglis, but now Mulder comes around to Carey, who clips off his pads to square leg for a single.
Back over the wicket, and Inglis cuts late for a couple more.
At the risk of putting the mockers on them, South Africa's bowlers have looked about as likely to take a wicket here as I would. Australia could be in for the long haul.
Inglis drives to Mulder, who fields off his own bowling.
He has to fend off his pads there though, slightly better line but easily handled by Inglis.
Record-breakers...
It's up at 161 runs now.
They'd have to go some to extend the partnership into a new calendar year though...
95th over - Jansen carries on
Good carry from Jansen, but comfortably left on length by Inglis outside off, the wicketkeeper-turned-fielder shouldering arms.
He gets a single next ball to get off strike.
Carey drives to cover, where Mulder does a brilliant diving stop to save a couple - they will run two.

Carey drives through cover again, this time a bit straighter and Mulder has to run a lot further. He gets there and stops the ball with his foot, almost tying himself in a knot deciding whether he would need to adjust his stride or should drive. This time they get three.
Inglis has to duck under a bouncer.
Inglis keeps the strike with a single to midwicket.
94th over - Mulder searching for the truth
He wants to believe that there's a wicket to be taken here.
He starts straight, with Rickelton up behind the stumps.
Solid defence from Inglis and then a sneaky single.
Around the wicket to left handed Carey who defends solidly.
Carey fends back the way the ball came from, Mulder back-handing it back to Rickelton at gentle pace.
Carey fends to square leg but there's no run there. He'll be OK taking his time.
Carey fends to cover - again there's no run.
93rd over - Marco Jansen is continuing
He was not quite in the best of health yesterday, like his strike bowling partner Rabada. But he is digging in here.
He starts short and Carey gets under it pretty comfortably.
Solid defence from Carey - Jansen is coming over the wicket to the left hander, but expect him to mix it up a bit over the next little while.
Carey just fends off his pad into square leg. No run, a firm shout from Carey ensuring that Inglis didn't think otherwise.

Bouncer, Jansen already looks irritated. It is hard to get a real read on the giant allrounder from Potchefstroom in the North West Province near Pretoria so he may be absolutely thrilled as well. Hard to tell.
Not a productive over for Australia, but the discipline of yesterday has carried over into this morning session and that's a great sign.
92nd over - Wiaan Mulder is starting things up from the other end
And that's not great news for South Africa.
Kagiso Rabada is out there, but perhaps still isn't right to bowl at express pace. The commentators are saying that he has a stomach bug.
Down the leg side, left alone by Inglis.
FOUR! Poor from Coetzee, who has not had the impact he would have liked coming into the side. He dived over the ball at mid on and the ball races away to the boundary. Sloppy.
Inglis defends.
Oh and that was closer, Inglis just getting an inside edge as he falls across to the off side, the ball nipping back into the Australian batter.
Only a single slip, who watches as Inglis defends.
A helmet has been called for, and that means that Ryan Rickelton is going to come up to the stumps and keep Inglis in his crease a bit more.
Lovely defence to end the over, high elbows and a straight bat.
91st over - Marco Jansen will start us off
It looks like a belter of a day out there in Cape Town. The colour of that sky is worth the subscription fee alone. The crags of Table Mountain jagged and vivid against the blue.
Marco Jansen is holding onto the ball from the Wynberg End.
He starts leg side to Alex Carey, who can't tickle it away to fine leg.
Better line, Carey defends solidly.
Only two slips, they both grimace as Carey defends with the inside half of his bat to a fuller ball by Jansen.
Nicely driven by Carey, a bit too wide from Jansen, and it's a single out to the boundary rider at deep cover.
Driven square by Inglis, a bit of a stretch for the sub wicket keeper, and a tad uppish, but safe enough for a single out to deep point.

INSIDE EDGE! Oh that is unlucky for Marco Jansen, and the sort of moment that might instantly plant dark thoughts into the minds of the Proteas, who had so many near misses yesterday. Carey was so close to chopping on there. He will run a couple after great fielding on the boundary.
Not much movement out there for the bowlers...
Steve Smith cleared of serious injury
Some positive news about Steve Smith.
Scans have confirmed that the veteran batter has suffered an injury to a cervical facet joint.
That is one of the joints that helps stabilise movement in the neck.

"Steve will continue to receive treatment and rehabilitation, with a full return to availability anticipated for the upcoming home Test series against New Zealand," Cricket Australia said in a statement.
That's good news, then.
Here's more about that.
A very good point

As thy say in the Classics - the first session will be crucial. Solid batting from Australia will go a long way to making it tough for South Africa. But a good session with the ball for South Africa and they could be right back in it. - NeilA

The first hour is going to be massive.
Australia has reason to be positive - unless someone left a sprinkler on overnight, this pitch won't have changed enough to be all that different from how it played yesterday.
But the Proteas could get their tails up with a good couple of overs with a new-ish ball in their hands.
If Rabada has recovered from whatever was ailing him yesterday, it could be a big test for Australia.
So important not to get ahead of themselves.
What did South Africa get wrong?
It's safe today that South Africa did not have the day they were hoping for yesterday.
So what went wrong?
There were a couple of slices of luck that went against them.

Opinion seems split on the catch that didn't carry that would have dismissed Cam Green, and the umpires call LBW shout on Matt Renshaw would have certainly knocked off the bails had he not got his pad in the way.
Then there were inside edges that missed the stumps, edges that flew over the slips... it was tough.
But South Africa didn't help themselves, either.
"There was effort there the whole day," Piet Botha, the Proteas' bowling coach, said. "Maybe if we're self critical, we didn't hit our length for long periods of time."

What a difference a day makes
Hello Simon and Chris, with the Aussie's four down, their nose in front and three 50+ partnerships on the board, the fans will start day three with less apprehension than yesterday... - Mike

It's incredible, isn't it Mike.
I think we all perhaps felt the worst was imminent when we were waiting the start yesterday.
But the patience of the batting has been really impressive.

Poor Marnus
Of course, Marnus Labuschagne has not had the best of days yesterday.
Another failure, on a pitch that is evidently brilliant to bat on, and his time in the Australian side surely must be limited.

"Marnus is a great mate of mine," Matt Renshaw said. "As batters, we can get out at any point and unfortunately today was a short one for him. "But from what I've seen in the first two Tests, he's been moving probably as well as I've seen him bat. "Unfortunately, sometimes you need a bit of luck and that's cricket. But the way he's going, I think he's very close."

Luck? There was a stat going around a few years back that Labuschagne was the luckiest of batters in Test cricket in terms of dropped catches and the like.
Perhaps the universe is evening things up for the unfortunate Queensland batter.
Cam Green's emotions in check
Playing his first Test of the series in Cape Town, Cameron Green had to come into the line up in the crucial number four batting spot.
But if he had any nerves, he did not show them.
After taking 15 balls to get off the mark, Green crushed a lofted cover drive off the final ball of the morning session from Marco Jansen.
Then, he smashed three boundaries off as many balls against the off-colour Kagiso Rabada.
Matt Renshaw noted that sort of flurry could have led to the tall all rounder losing his head.
"At times, if you hit a few boundaries in a row, you get a bit giddy," Renshaw said.
"So it's just about calming him down and sort of getting him to think about the process.
"I get along really well with Cam off the field, so that helps, but it's obviously different stages [the pair were at].
"I was in for probably an hour and a half before Cam came in, so I'm at a completely different mindset and tempo compared to when he's come in.
"He's pretty fresh, he's buzzing around a lot. So it's just about me being the calmer head out there, trying to calm him down.

"There's a few times where we sort of had some conversations [asking] what was going on there, and it was just about calming each other down, relaxing each other, and just trying to keep our tempos as much as we could."

Carey has got all of the ability in the world and, when he bats they way he batted yesterday, has all the potential to score big.

Renshaw, the opener hiding in plain sight
Partnerships win prizes
Day two was unquestionably Australia's.
Just four wickets falling.
Four batters getting half centuries.
A first innings lead.
It couldn't have gone much better.
And it's all down to the delivery of some big partnerships, two century stands and a half century opening pairing among them.

Anyone who has watched Test cricket over the last few years may have been stunned by the competency shown by the batting unit yesterday.
In fact, it was almost historic.
Four batters getting half centuries without Steve Smith, David Warner or Usman Khawaja being one of them in nearly 13 years is quite remarkable.
Analysis: The future for Australia is right now

The vague suspicion before play on day two of the Cape Town Test was that Australia — out of form, stalked by rumours of disharmony in the ranks, its batting line-up restocked and reshuffled for the umpteenth time — was one more calamitous batting collapse away from the end of an era.

The day of perfectly calm and controlled Test batting that took place instead was no less arresting, and in the context of this topsy-turvy series, far more surprising. For 90 overs, Australia batted diligently, adaptively, intelligently and at changing tempos, building a series of reassuring partnerships that put it in control of the game.
